description: The other ten title arms of the twelve-arm `replication-claim-title`, split off from `replication-claim-title-strong` (arms 3 and 6) so the two halves can be promoted and priced separately. Carried verbatim except arm 1, see below. On the current release these ten arms account for the balance of the family's 10,304 newly-admissible rows: the strong pair takes 4,237, arms {2,3,6,10} together take 9,211, and arm 2 (`replication stud(y|ies)`) alone is 5,078 of them — this half is mostly arm 2. WHAT THE LABELS SAY, arm by arm, from the blind Sonnet pass of 2026-08-04 (apparent precision, unclear counted as a miss): arm 2 89.6% (n=222) — the large, respectable one, and the one that carries most of this half's FLoRA recall; arm 10 `replication attempt(s)` 90.0% (n=20); arm 5 fail/attempt-to-replicate 70.8% (n=24); arm 11 failure nouns 50.0% (n=20); arm 4 `study replicate[sd]` 37.5% (n=8); arm 9 `success* replicat*` 25.0% (n=20); arm 12 the negation matrix 20.0% (n=20); arm 1 5.0% (n=20). Arms 7 and 8 have n=1 and n=2 and are unmeasured, not endorsed. Read the small-n arms as directional only: 20 labels bound nothing tightly. ARM 1 IS FIXED AND STILL SUSPECT. `we replicat(e|es|ed)` was firing on interrogative titles — "Can we replicate the European Post-War Transition?", "Why do we replicate?", "How often do we replicate previous research?" — which are meta-discussion, not a paper describing itself. The arm now requires the phrase to be followed by a run of non-punctuation and then either a non-question punctuation mark or the end of the title (`[^.?!;:]*(?:[.!;:]|$)`): it fires only when the next punctuation mark after the phrase is not a question mark. Written positively because specs must be RE2-safe — the engine's validator rejects lookahead — and verified row-for-row identical to the lookahead form over the arm's 23 pool rows, so a question anywhere later in the title (after a period, colon or semicolon) is correctly left alone. Measured: 18 of the arm's 23 pool rows are excluded. BUT THE FIX DOES NOT RESCUE THE ARM — all 5 surviving labelled rows are labelled no (stellar nucleosynthesis, propagated replicate populations, waveform statistics: the experimental-replicate and terminology_only senses), and the single `yes` among the arm's 20 labels was itself interrogative ("Can we replicate the findings of EEF trials…?") and is removed by the fix. On this evidence arm 1 admits 5 rows and no known true positives, and the honest next step is deleting it rather than repairing it; it is kept here, shadowed, so that decision rests on its own diagnostic rather than on n=20. PRECEDENCE 740: below `replication-claim-title-strong` (750) because it is the measurably weaker half of the same claim, above `replication-claim-text` (730) because a title claim is still positional — a title is the paper's own statement of what it is — and above `not-a-study-type` (500) for the reason the whole family outranks it. A free number was taken rather than renumbering a neighbour (CONVENTIONS.md, "Precedence"). `vocabulary` null, as across the family. OPEN: promoting this half is a recall decision, not a precision one. It roughly doubles the family's FLoRA capture for about $10 more of screening, and the screen exists to reject exactly the false positives these arms admit — but it also feeds Stage 3, where volume is the real cost. D3 (planned-but-not-completed replications, arm 7's `aim|set out to replicate`) is inherited unresolved.
